items.name: Forecast window
items.value: 30 days after the 2023-02-06 mainshock
items.detail: The modified Omori law estimates the expected aftershock count over days 0–30.

items.name: Aftershock rate
items.value: Modified Omori law; MLE grid c=0.01–1.00 by 0.01 and p=0.80–1.60 by 0.01
items.detail: The catalog time sequence is modeled as a point process; K is estimated in closed form for each c,p pair.

items.name: Magnitude frequencies
items.value: Gutenberg–Richter fit; 0.2 magnitude bin width
items.detail: Normalized 10^(-bM) weights are used to weight candidate magnitude bins.

items.name: Ground motion
items.value: BSSA14 PGA; observed epicentral distance used as a point-source proxy for Rjb
items.detail: Uses site Vs30 and the published BSSA14 median and heteroscedastic sigma; no finite-fault geometry is available for these aftershocks.

items.name: Unsafe threshold
items.detail: P(unsafe) is the Poisson exceedance probability over the 30-day window. The same threshold screens TMCs in the risk-aware deterministic model.

items.name: TMC capacity
items.value: clip(site_area_m2 / 30, 30, 2,000)
items.detail: Uses outdoor site/campus polygon area at 30 m² per person, with minimum and maximum capacity bounds. Type-based defaults are a fallback when area is missing.

items.name: Fallback TMC capacities
items.value: school 200; university 300; sports centre 250; stadium 500; social facility 100
items.detail: Applied only when site area is unavailable.

items.name: Existing hospital capacity
items.value: Curated bed_capacity_total; effective_capacity_postquake when present
items.detail: Closed hospitals with zero effective post-quake capacity are excluded from usable capacity.

items.name: Hospital-to-site matching
items.value: Nearest OSM hospital site within 25 km
items.detail: Used to match curated hospitals to OSM hospital features and exclude duplicate TMC candidates.

models.name: Risk-blind deterministic MILP
models.summary: Facility location and casualty allocation without aftershock hazard screening.

items.name: Demand
items.value: Casualty scenario 1; all periods are aggregated
items.detail: Every demand point must be fully allocated to a hospital or selected TMC.

items.name: Objective
items.value: distance_km × assigned casualties + 1,000 per opened TMC
items.detail: The opening penalty is a judgment-chosen tradeoff, not a monetary facility cost. C_TRANS=1 defines the objective units.

items.name: Candidate eligibility
items.value: All prepared TMC candidates
items.detail: No PGA safety exclusion is applied.

models.name: Risk-aware deterministic MILP
models.summary: Same deterministic facility-location model, with an aftershock PGA eligibility screen.

items.name: Demand and objective
items.value: Same as risk-blind deterministic MILP
items.detail: Scenario 1 demand is aggregated; travel burden is minimized with a 1,000 casualty-km opening penalty per TMC.

items.name: Candidate eligibility
items.value: Exclude candidates with representative PGA > 0.2
items.detail: The representative value is the maximum median PGA for significant observed aftershocks. This is a deterministic screen, separate from P(unsafe).

models.name: Scenario-wise Paper LP
models.summary: Solves one continuous medical response LP for each of 20 casualty scenarios.

items.name: Scenario weights
items.value: 20 source scenarios; uses scenario_prob values supplied in the casualty file (must sum to 1)
items.detail: Results are reported per scenario and probability-weighted for summaries.

items.name: Optimization priorities
items.value: Lexicographic: minimize unmet casualties (Z1), then travel (Z2), then additional staff (Z3)
items.detail: There is no first-stage TMC opening decision; positive-flow candidate sites are not explicit openings.

items.name: T1 routing limit
items.detail: T1 casualties route only to existing hospitals within the effective distance limit; TMCs do not receive T1 casualties.

items.name: Health-state transitions
items.value: Treated and untreated triage transition matrices

items.name: Staff productivity
items.value: 4 patients per doctor and 8 per nurse
items.detail: Additional doctors and nurses are decision variables; productivity values are explicitly documented planning assumptions.

items.name: Existing and additional staff
items.value: Existing hospital doctors/nurses are available at their input counts; extra staff is optimized
items.detail: TMCs begin with no base staff in the model. Extra doctors and nurses are continuous decision variables.

items.name: Capacity under damage
items.value: Hospital capacity loss = local damage × 0.50 × scenario severity; TMC outpatient capacity = 3 × TMC bed capacity
items.detail: TMC bed capacity uses the shared area-derived rule. TMC capacity is not reduced by the hospital damage factor.

models.name: Two-stage SAA
models.summary: Chooses a TMC policy under site-count budgets, then evaluates allocation and staffing recourse on sampled scenarios.

items.name: Sampling
items.value: 20 source scenarios with uniform probability; final profile uses 10 replications × 10 training scenarios and 1,000 out-of-sample draws
items.detail: Random seed 20261002; the dashboard reports only profiles present in the selected run export.

items.name: TMC budgets
items.detail: The SAA policy selects within each site-count budget; TOPSIS candidate pool is limited to 120 when selected.

items.name: Casualty uncertainty
items.value: Mean-one lognormal multiplier, sigma 0.20
items.detail: Applied to scenario casualty demand in sampled runs.

items.name: Road and hospital damage
items.value: Road multiplier ~ Uniform(0, 0.30); hospital capacity loss = local damage × Uniform(0, 0.50)
items.detail: Each SAA draw samples one road multiplier applied to all demand-facility pairs and one damage-loss multiplier per hospital. Unlike Paper LP, these SAA damage draws are not scaled by source-scenario severity.

items.name: Health transitions
items.value: Untreated triage transitions only; treated-state transitions are not modeled in SAA
items.detail: Untreated: T1→D/T1 = 0.60/0.40; T2→T1/T2 = 0.55/0.45; T3→T2/T3 = 0.25/0.75. Treated casualties leave the untreated pool, but SAA does not model the Paper LP's treated-state progression or facility occupancy recursion.

items.name: T1 routing and staffing
items.value: T1 can go only to hospitals within 12 km; 4 patients per doctor and 8 per nurse per period
items.detail: Existing hospital staff counts are used where available; additional staffing is optimized. TMCs start with no base staff.

items.name: Capacity and objective weights
items.value: Per-period capacity limits; unmet penalty = 10 × (maximum transport cost + maximum staffing cost); travel weight 1 per casualty-km; extra-staff weight 1,000 per staff-period
items.detail: Capacity is held constant across periods within each scenario. Hospital capacity is reduced by scenario damage; TMC T3 capacity is 3× its bed capacity. SAA has no separate TMC opening-cost term.
